title: An 80-Million-Year-Old Shark Graveyard Was Found in the Egyptian Desert
mediaSource: Egypt Western Desert shark fossil teeth, Abu Tartur Plateau desert, Cretaceous shark fossils, ancient tropical sea North Africa

scenes.title: Shark teeth were found in the middle of a desert
scenes.narration: In Egypt's nearly waterless Western Desert, scientists found a cluster of fossil shark teeth dating back roughly 80 million years. The researchers described the site as a shark graveyard.

scenes.title: The find included 14 fossil teeth
scenes.narration: Researchers analyzed 14 fossil shark teeth from phosphate-rich rocks on Egypt's Abu Tartur Plateau. The new study identified at least five extinct shark species in the assemblage.
keywords: fossil shark teeth close up museum

scenes.title: Today's desert was once a tropical sea
scenes.narration: During the Late Cretaceous, when these fossils were deposited, what is now western Egypt was covered by a warm tropical sea. Higher sea levels submerged large parts of North Africa.

scenes.title: At least seven shark species are known from the area
scenes.narration: Combining the new finds with earlier records, scientists now know of at least seven shark species from this part of the formation. That points to a rich marine ecosystem capable of supporting many large predators.

scenes.title: One may be the first record of its kind in Africa
scenes.narration: A shark related to today's goblin shark, Scapanorhynchus raphiodon, may represent the first fossil record of that taxon in Africa. Several other species were also reported from Egypt for the first time.
keywords: goblin shark close up real photo

scenes.title: The desert still remembers an ancient ocean
scenes.narration: Today the region is sand and rock, but beneath it are traces of a sea where sharks once swam. Fossils can preserve the story of an environment long after the landscape has completely changed.
keywords: shark fossil teeth in rock close up
